lens: LUCK AND MULTIPLE COMPARISONS (permutation within game-day, game-cluster CIs, leave-one-game-out, Bonferroni / family-wise haircut)
rule: R7 Wait-and-confirm: after an R1 trigger (first c/w look 2-360 min before the start with EV >= 2.5%) wait 5 minutes and buy only if still listed (any source, freshest listing look <= 7 min old, >= 2 min to the start) with the last c/w price look EV >= 2.5%; price = that look's
numbers_reproduced: Reproduced exactly. R1 triggers 184 bets (44 games, 116 with a close). After 5 min: 55 dropped, 36 listed with EV < 2.5%, 16 past/too close to the start, 77 confirmed (28 games). R7 CLV at the T+5 price = +2.93% on 52 closes / 25 games, game-cluster 95% CI [+1.92, +3.79] (builder [+1.99, +3.81], same mean to 12 digits; the CI differs only by bootstrap seed/size); close_ok only +3.08% on 50/24g. Same bets at their trigger price +2.77% (builder baseline 2.7686%). Whole R1 (the parent, buy every trigger at once) +2.54% [+1.77, +3.52] on 116 closes/40 games. Not confirmed +2.36% on 64/32g. Halves by decision day: Oct 3 +1.78% (17 closes/14g, CI [+0.02, +3.91]); Oct 4-5 +3.49% (35/17g, [+2.84, +4.22]); builder 2.32 / 3.06 on a slightly different cut. ROI at the first-listed price -16.8% on 73 settled / 26 games, CI [-45.1, +11.6] (builder -16.1% at the look price). The question for the rule is not CLV vs 0 but confirmed vs the parent R1: +0.41 pts [-1.62, +1.79], bootstrap p(<=0) 0.357 (builder 0.36).
reason: The rule's whole CLV (+2.9%) is R1's EV >= 2.5% gate, not the 5-minute confirmation; what the confirmation adds (+0.41 pts per bet, +0.16 pts of it from the T+5 price) cannot be told from luck, and it is the wrong sign on independent closes. (1) Permutation, same-sized subsets of the R1 closed triggers drawn within start day, 5000 draws: null mean 2.49% sd 0.39%; p(null >= observed) = 0.135 at the T+5 price, 0.244 at the trigger price (within trigger day 0.129/0.237; no strata 0.163/0.293). Whole-game redraws (games drawn at random from the 40 R1 games until 52 closes): p 0.255 / 0.335. The observed CLV sits at percentile 86 of the null (builder's permutation p 0.14: reproduced). Against broader universes (random same-size draws from the 378 first-in-window c/w closes, mean +0.82%, or all 683 closed bets, mean +0.19%) p < 0.0002, but that only re-measures the EV gate that R1 already carries. (2) Multiple comparisons: p 0.135-0.24 x 15 hypothesis families = 1.0 (capped); x 522 variants = 1.0. Family-wise test over 32 R7 variants (wait 2,3,5,7,10,15,20,30 min x confirm threshold 2.0,2.5,3.0,3.5%), max-t under within-day shuffles of CLV, 4000 draws: R7's own t = 0.58, family-wise p = 0.92 (the median max-t of the null is 1.65, its 95th percentile 3.20). The best neighbour (wait 3 min, EV >= 3.0%, 35 confirmed closes) has t 2.97, diff +2.0 pts, family-wise p 0.074: not significant either, and it is not R7. Only 22 of 32 variants have a positive difference and 9 have t > 1.64 (about 1.6 expected if the variants were independent, but they overlap heavily; they are all waits of 2-7 minutes); the effect disappears at 10+ minutes (diffs -0.03 to -1.4 pts). (3) Game clustering: CI of the difference [-1.62, +1.79] includes 0; within-game fixed-effect estimate (17 games with both confirmed and not-confirmed closed bets) +1.14 pts [-1.01, +2.49], p(<=0) 0.135. (4) Not driven by one or two games (leave-one-game-out CLV +2.77% to +3.24% over 25 closed games, the largest game holds 9 of the 52 closes; dropping the top 3 games by contribution +2.60% [1.46, 3.73] on 37/22g), but that robustness belongs to R1's level, not to the confirmation. (5) The close source drives the level: of the 52 closes 38 are Tracker closes (a re-read of CNO's own books before the start, i.e. the same consensus that produced the listed EV, so CLV tracks listed EV by construction): +4.14% [+3.22, +4.95], 95% beat. Independent closes (ESPN, Pinnacle, Novig trades with 3+ trades) are 12 closes / 10 games: -0.26% [-1.61, +1.54], 58% beat; 1-2-trade Novig closes 2. On the independent closes confirmed is WORSE than not confirmed: -0.26% (12/10g) vs +1.42% (21/14g), diff -1.68 pts [-3.76, +0.18], p(>=) 0.91; whole R1 on independent closes only +0.81% [-0.04, +2.10] on 33/23g. (6) Halves disagree in sign for the confirmation effect: confirmed minus not confirmed -0.81 pts on Oct 3 (17 vs 14 closes) and +0.96 pts on Oct 4-5 (35 vs 50), neither significant (game-cluster bootstrap p(diff <= 0) 0.73 on Oct 3 and 0.22 on Oct 4-5). (7) Cost: R7 keeps 77 of 184 triggers: 34.1 bets a day vs 81.6 for R1, i.e. 1.00 vs 2.08 CLV-units a day (bets x mean CLV): half the expected edge for +0.4 pts a bet that is not distinguishable from 0. 55 of the 184 triggers (30%) are no longer listed after 5 min; the 107 not-confirmed triggers (64 with a close) still carry +2.36%. (8) What the 5-minute price change adds is tiny: paired T+5-price minus trigger-price CLV +0.16 pts [+0.01, +0.38] over 25 games (sign-flip p 0.048 one-sided, 0.096 two-sided; only 11.5% of the 52 bets changed price, 9.6% better, 1.9% worse): a small gain that rests on 6 of 52 bets changing price (it is the price-improvement tail, not the confirmation). Verdict: not a credible improvement over just buying every R1 trigger; the data suggests the confirmation does nothing detectable, and a Bonferroni-corrected p is 1.0. It would take about 1330 closed R1 triggers per arm (about 2,660 closed triggers, about 52 days at R1's 51 closes a day, ICC about 0 so no design effect) to detect +0.41 pts at 80% power and a two-sided 5% level; about 225 per arm (about 9 days) if the true gain were +1.0 pt.
caveats: Effective sample: 52 closes / 25 games for R7 over ~2.26 days of first-looks (decision days Oct 3-5); 'out of sample' means the second half of ~2 days.

Builder and I agree to 12 digits on CLV (2.9316%) and on the 77/55/36/16 split when the freshest look of any kind (including book-page 'k' looks) sets the listing age; counting only listing looks gives 76 confirmed (1 bet with no close moves between the stale and confirmed groups).

The permutation shuffles bets within start day, which ignores game clustering and is lenient (anti-conservative); the game-cluster bootstrap p (0.357) and whole-game redraw p (0.255-0.335) are the more honest ones, and both are weaker. A pattern-swap game-block permutation (13 start-day x game-size classes) was run but its null mean is +0.88 pts (one large 26-bet game cannot move), so it is not used as evidence (one-sided p 0.83).
R1's per-trigger CLV has intra-game correlation near zero (ICC -0.006, n=116 closes / 40 games), so game clustering matters little for the bet-level tests here.

Tracker closes are 75 of R1's 116 closes and 38 of R7's 52: a CLV measured against a re-read of the same CNO books is partly circular; the independent-close sample (12 for R7, 33 for R1) is far too small to say R7 is bad, only that nothing supports it.
tried_count 522 (builder): the family-wise test here covers only the 32 R7 variants, so it understates the true multiplicity; with 15 hypothesis families the corrected p is already capped at 1.0.

Short waits (2-3 min) show larger confirmed-vs-not differences (+1.2 to +2.0 pts, n = 66-77 closed confirmed) that fade by 10 minutes: a candidate for a pre-registered check on new data, not for the app; family-wise p of the best variant is 0.074.
ROI is noise at this size (73 settled bets, CI [-45%, +12%]); it neither supports nor refutes the rule.
Any change to what is bought is a QUESTION FOR TJ, not an action; this rule would only ever remove bets (it loosens no safety limit).
